- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is high (especially >0.5) — reduce initial forecast by 1–2% for high sentiment.
- Underestimate late-period spikes (especially >85) when sentiment is low (especially <0.3) — add 1–3% buffer to late forecast values.
- Overshoot after sharp sentiment spikes — cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak if sentiment drops sharply post-peak.
- Mean-revert forecasts toward 78–82 range if sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.4) over 3–5 days — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- Lagged forecast errors are most common in 10–15 day horizon — apply 1–2% downward correction if true outcome is >10% above forecast at that point.
- High sentiment + low historical volatility → overconfidence bias — reduce forecast by 1–2% for high sentiment + low recent price range.
